name: Skyrmion racetrack drive
subtitle: an archive drive with no moving parts

effects.effect: tiny stable magnetic whirls can be pushed along a wire with very little current
a current of spin-aligned electrons can flip a tiny magnet

effect: tiny stable magnetic whirls can be pushed along a wire with very little current
how: Data centres keep most of the world's data on spinning hard disks, which wear out and use power just to keep turning. Here each bit is a tiny magnetic whirl lined up along a nanowire, and pulses of spin-aligned current slide the whole row past a reading head like beads on a string, packing disk-like capacity into a chip with no motor.
obstacle: Skyrmions drift sideways and snag on tiny flaws as they move, so the rows lose their spacing.
why: Racetrack memory proposed in 2008; no working skyrmion drive exists.
real: Room-temperature writing, current-driven motion and MTJ readout of skyrmions shown as separate lab components; no working racetrack memory.
